I'm a 60-year-old woman, been farming these fields for 36 years, never went to school. My old man and me, we have 15 mu of land and only the two of us to work it. We grow wheat and maize on 10 mu — wheat in winter, then maize right after — and 5 mu of cotton because cotton brings more money, but you can't grow too much because picking it by hand takes forever.

**How I think about this year**

I don't read books and I don't trust those extension people who come with their papers. I trust what I see. Last year my neighbor tried to save money on fertilizer and his wheat came up thin like a sick chicken. I won't make that mistake. I know one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and when the wheat turns yellow at jointing, I put down half a bag of urea. That's what I've done for years and it works. My wheat usually gives me around 450 jin per mu, sometimes 500 if the rain is good.

For the maize, there's no time to waste after wheat harvest. The combine cuts the wheat, and within two or three days the maize has to go in or you miss the season. I don't plow — no time for that. I plant the hybrid seed, put compound fertilizer in the hole, and pray for rain. If it doesn't rain in July, I pump water once. More than that and the pumping cost eats your profit.

The cotton is on the other 5 mu. We plant in late April, rotary till the soil first. Cotton needs more medicine — insects love cotton. I spray herbicide once and insecticide two or three times. I also give it some fertilizer when it flowers. Picking is the hard part. At our age, bending down all day hurts the back. I hire a few women from the village for the main picking, about 5 days total. It costs money but we can't do it all ourselves anymore.

Money is tight. I have to buy seeds, fertilizer, diesel for the pump, medicine for the crops, and pay the hired hands. I keep some cash aside for emergencies — if I spend everything on fertilizer and then someone gets sick, we're in trouble. So I don't buy the fancy stuff. I buy what's available at the shop in town, the same as always.

I never calculate kilos exactly. I know a 50-jin bag. I know my fields. That's enough.
